A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same quantization-induced unlearning failure study and SURE method. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantization and SURE experiments on NEWS and BOOKS, with additional RWKU results, sensitivity analysis, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original quantization and SURE results in Tables 1–3 and its appendices, including RWKU evaluation, hyperparameter analysis, and ablations.

M1.justification: SURE retains the same large learning rate, gradient-based module saliency, thresholding, and masked parameter updates in Equations (4)–(6). The revised introduction changes its positioning, not its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use NEWS, BOOKS, RWKU, and the same utility tasks: MMLU, TruthfulQA, TriviaQA, and AlpacaEval. The added main-text pointer to RWKU refers to evaluation already present in v2 Appendix F.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same GA/NPO variants, target/retrained references, RT, RMU, and RMU_LAT, alongside the same quantization methods. The new pointer to v3 Appendix J references experiments already reported in v2 Appendix I.

E3.justification: The models, dataset construction, metrics, shot counts, training epochs, optimizer, hyperparameter searches, and quantization settings remain unchanged in Sections 4 and 6.2 and Appendices C–D. No revised evaluation protocol is documented.

E4.justification: The NEWS saliency-threshold sweep moves unchanged from Section 6.2 and Table 4 to Appendix H and Table 9. The SURE/S component ablation in Table 10 is also retained unchanged; neither analysis is newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The new sensitivity warning does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched result tables retain the same entries and numerical values, including quantization comparisons, SURE, RWKU, ablations, and the relocated hyperparameter results. The headline 21% versus 83% knowledge-retention finding is also unchanged.

T1.justification: The unlearning objectives, quantization-interval reasoning, saliency definitions, and metric formulas in Equations (1)–(13) remain unchanged. No mathematical assumption, proof, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction recasts the third contribution from proposing and validating a countermeasure to an initial mitigation effort intended to inspire further research. This modestly narrows the main-text framing, consistent with language already in v2 Appendix J; the central failure claim, abstract, and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 newly warns in the introduction that the framework is highly sensitive to hyperparameter selection, leading to an unstable unlearned model. v2 discussed utility trade-offs and contained the same sensitivity analysis, but did not explicitly state this limitation.

D1.justification: The reproducibility appendix replaces v2's anonymous repository link with the GitHub address already present in both abstracts. This corrects access instructions without establishing newly available code. Implementation details and hyperparameter values remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Li et al. (2024c, 2025) and Wang et al. (2024a–c), foregrounds the existing localization-informed lineage in the introduction, and adds explicit attribution to Lynch et al. in the robustness discussion. The broader related-work analysis remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized introduction rewrites, additional cross-references, and an acknowledgment accompany moving the hyperparameter subsection into Appendix H and renumbering subsequent appendices. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 Table 4 moves from the main text to v3 Appendix H as Table 9, with associated table relocation and page reflow. Both figures and all table designs remain substantially unchanged. Blue highlighting in some appendix text and headings is removed.

improvement.justification: v3 makes SURE's provisional role and hyperparameter sensitivity clearer in the introduction and aligns the reproducibility appendix's code-access instructions with the abstract. The sensitivity evidence becomes less prominent after moving to Appendix H but remains intact. With methods, theory, and results unchanged, the improvement is limited to clearer qualification and documentation.
